reading.body:
CyrusOne Sterling (NVA4) is a small existing data center in Virginia, publishing 11 MW of IT capacity, which places it 22nd of 25 disclosed facilities and outside the tier shaping AI scaling bottlenecks.

The facility's 11 MW across 128,715 square feet of technical space implies roughly 275 racks at a common AI training density of 40 kW per rack. That is a modest footprint for AI workloads, which concentrate far more power per building. It holds 0.7% of Virginia's disclosed 1,603 MW, so it is not among the large sites that drive compute scaling.

Virginia has 330 mapped data center facilities, but most publish no capacity data, making the disclosed set sparse and rankings potentially understate the market. For NVA4, the missing inputs matter more: no grid supply, interconnection queue position, announced expansion, or certifications are published. Those are the factors that would determine whether it can add power or support AI-scale compute, and they are absent here.
